raw_response:
Let me think this through like I always do at the start of the season.

I have 10.1 mu, and I do wheat-maize every year like everybody here in Quzhou. Last year went okay, so I will mostly do the same thing. Changing too much is risky — if I mess up, my family of 7 still has to eat.

**Winter wheat first (already planted last October, will harvest June):**
I put down 2 bags of 复合肥 (compound fertilizer, 15-15-15, 50 kg bag) per mu when I plowed — that's about 15 kg N, 15 kg P, 15 kg K per mu from the base. At jointing time in spring I will topdress with about 1 bag of urea (50 kg) across 3 mu, so roughly 15-17 kg urea per mu — that adds maybe 7-8 kg more N. Total N around 22 kg/mu. My neighbor Old Wang does similar.

Seeds — I buy improved hybrid type from the agro-shop, everyone around here does. Jimai or Shiluan kind of varieties.

Irrigation for wheat: I pump from the well 3 times — winter water before freeze, one at returning green/jointing, one at heading. Maybe a 4th if spring is very dry, but water costs electricity money.

Pesticide on wheat: spray 2 times — once for weeds in spring, once for aphids and rust near heading. Sometimes a 3rd if aphids are bad.

Tillage for wheat: rotary after the maize comes off, fast and cheap, everyone does it this way.

Expected wheat yield: around 450 kg/mu if weather is normal. Last year I got close to that.

**Summer maize (plant in June right after wheat):**
Direct seed into the wheat stubble — no-till, saves diesel and time. I buy Zhengdan or Denghai hybrid seed from the dealer.

Fertilizer for maize: 1.5 bags of compound fertilizer per mu at planting (~11 kg N, 11 kg P, 11 kg K), then topdress with urea at big-bell stage, about 20 kg urea/mu = 9 kg N. Total N around 20 kg/mu.

Irrigation for maize: usually 1-2 times if July-August rain is not enough. Here rain is usually okay in summer so 1 time on average.

Pesticide on maize: 1-2 sprays — mostly for corn borer and armyworm. Sometimes weeds if herbicide at seeding didn't hold.

Expected maize yield: 550 kg/mu, pretty reliable around here.

I would rather put a little extra fertilizer than lose yield — a bad harvest hurts the family much more than spending a few extra yuan on urea.
